tools.name: mobile_list_available_devices
tools.description: List all available devices. This includes both physical devices and simulators. If there is more than one device returned, you need to let the user select one of them.

tools.name: mobile_use_device
tools.description: Select a device to use. This can be a simulator or an Android device. Use the list_available_devices tool to get a list of available devices.

device.description: The name of the device to select

deviceType.description: The type of device to select

tools.name: mobile_list_apps
tools.description: List all the installed apps on the device

tools.name: mobile_launch_app
tools.description: Launch an app on mobile device. Use this to open a specific app. You can find the package name of the app by calling list_apps_on_device.

packageName.description: The package name of the app to launch

tools.name: mobile_terminate_app
tools.description: Stop and terminate an app on mobile device

packageName.description: The package name of the app to terminate

tools.name: mobile_get_screen_size
tools.description: Get the screen size of the mobile device in pixels

tools.name: mobile_learn_app_context_and_navigation_guidelines
tools.description: Reads previously saved app context and navigation guidelines and returns them so they can be used to navigate through the app before generating test steps.

tools.name: guidelines_to_write_code
tools.description: Read coding guidelienes from ~/guardian/.cursor/rules/mcp-production-grade.json and return them so they can be followed when writing code. These guidelines include coding standards, best practices, patterns to follow, and anti-patterns to avoid. They are mandatory to follow when writing code. NOTE: Only write code after app exploration is complete and locators are fetched.

tools.name: debug_dump_xml_structure
tools.description: DEBUG: Dump the raw parsed XML structure to see how fast-xml-parser creates the object

tools.name: mobile_list_elements_on_screen
tools.description: List elements on screen in a simplified, flattened structure. Returns only useful attributes: text, class, id (resource-id), accessibilityId (content-desc), and bounds. Do not cache this result.

tools.name: mobile_press_button
tools.description: Press a button on device

button.description: The button to press. Supported buttons: BACK (android only), HOME, VOLUME_UP, VOLUME_DOWN, ENTER, DPAD_CENTER (android tv only), DPAD_UP (android tv only), DPAD_DOWN (android tv only), DPAD_LEFT (android tv only), DPAD_RIGHT (android tv only)

tools.name: mobile_open_deeplink
tools.description: Open a deeplink in app on device

tools.name: scroll_on_screen
tools.description: Scroll on the screen. IMPORTANT: Don't scroll continuously 2 times to avoid missing elements. After each scroll, call mobile_list_elements_on_screen tool to check what is currently visible on screen before scrolling again.

direction.description: The scroll direction: 'up' scrolls up to reveal content above (swipe down gesture), 'down' scrolls down to reveal content below (swipe up gesture)

tools.name: mobile_type_keys
tools.description: Type text into the focused element

submit.description: Whether to submit the text. If true, the text will be submitted as if the user pressed the enter key.

tools.name: mobile_set_orientation
tools.description: Change the screen orientation of the device

tools.name: mobile_get_orientation
tools.description: Get the current screen orientation of the device

tools.name: mobile_tap_by_text
tools.description: Tap an element on screen by any attribute: text, accessibilityId (content-desc), or id (resource-id). Searches all attributes automatically.

value.description: The value to search for - can be text, accessibilityId, or id

tools.name: mobile_fetch_jira_ticket
tools.description: Fetch JIRA ticket information including summary, description, and extract Figma links from description

tools.name: mobile_export_figma_png
tools.description: Export Figma file as PNG

figmaUrl.description: The Figma file URL to export as PNG

tools.name: fetch_testcases_from_tcms
tools.description: Before calling these tool, folder name can be analysed by data fetched from jira ticket info. Before generating test cases for a jira ticket, always fetch existing test cases from TCMS tool for a specific folder

folderName.description: The folder name to filter test cases (e.g., PDP), folder name can to be fetched from jira ticket info

tools.name: generate_testcases_from_ticket_data
tools.description: Generate manual test cases by analyzing PNG design with JIRA requirements

tools.name: check_testcases_status
tools.description: Check if test cases have been generated and saved to file

tools.name: review_testcases
tools.description: Open test cases in browser for manual approval.

testCases.description: test cases array generated by tool generate_testcases_from_ticket_data

tools.name: check_approval_status
tools.description: Check the approval status of test cases review session (waits 25 seconds before checking)

tools.name: update_testcases_to_tcms
tools.description: Create new test cases in TCMS from approved test cases. Only processes test cases with 'New' status, ignores Modify and Remove cases since APIs are not available.

testCases.description: Array of test case arrays from approved test cases

tools.name: browserstack_create_subfolder
tools.description: Create a sub-folder inside a parent folder in BrowserStack Test Management. Use this after classifying test cases by feature to create a named sub-folder for that feature.

parentFolderId.description: Numeric ID of the parent folder in which to create the sub-folder

tools.name: browserstack_get_test_cases
tools.description: Fetch all test cases inside a folder from BrowserStack Test Management. Returns identifier, title, and folder_id for each test case so the LLM can classify them into features.

folderId.description: Numeric ID of the folder whose test cases should be fetched

tools.name: browserstack_bulk_move_test_cases
tools.description: Bulk move test cases into a destination folder in BrowserStack Test Management. Use this after classifying test cases and creating the target sub-folder. Supports up to 1000 test case IDs per call.

testCaseIds.description: Array of test case identifiers to move, e.g. ["TC-0042", "TC-0188"]

destinationFolderId.description: Numeric ID of the destination folder
